issues.failure_explanation: Equation (21) asserts that \tau_{i^*} \ge -\rho \ge \tau_{j^*}. However, by the KKT optimality conditions shown in Table 1, every element of \Iup satisfies \tau_i \le -\rho, implying \tau_{i^*} = \max_{i \in \Iup} \tau_i \le -\rho, while every element of \Idown satisfies \tau_j \ge -\rho, implying \tau_{j^*} = \min_{j \in \Idown} \tau_j \ge -\rho. Therefore, the true KKT bounds satisfy \tau_{i^*} \le -\rho \le \tau_{j^*}. Both inequalities in (21) are reversed, which also leads to the erroneous statement in Section 7.1 that -\rho lies in [\tau_{j^*}, \tau_{i^*}].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the inequality signs in (21) to \tau_{i^*} \le -\rho \le \tau_{j^*} and update the corresponding prose in Section 7.1 to state that -\rho lies in [\tau_{i^*}, \tau_{j^*}].
issues.overall_effect: The stated bounds on -\rho in Remark 3 and the interval rationale motivating the shrinking criteria in Section 7.1 are mathematically inverted.
issues.title: Reversed bounding inequalities for optimal threshold in bias recovery and shrinking
issues.why_classification: Correcting the inequality directions is a local repair that preserves the midpoint heuristic formula and the rest of the algorithm without requiring new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 3 asserts that variables \alpha_k^* = 0 are easier to freeze compared to the corresponding \alpha-criterion \eqref{eq:s1} because the effective threshold is \tau_{i^*} - 2y_k\varepsilon/100 < \tau_{i^*}. However, criterion \eqref{eq:s1} for \alpha_k = 0 is \tau_k < \tau_{j^*}, which is an upper bound on \tau_k involving \tau_{j^*}, whereas \tau_{i^*} comes from criterion \eqref{eq:s2} for \alpha_k = C_k. Similarly, for \alpha_k^* = C_k, the threshold is compared to \tau_{j^*} from \eqref{eq:s1} rather than \eqref{eq:s2}. The comparison cross-matches upper-bound and lower-bound variables with opposite inequality directions, making the claimed comparative ease of freezing mathematically unsupported.

failure_location.quote:
Compared with the corresponding $\alpha$-criteria~\eqref{eq:s1}--\eqref{eq:s2}:
variables $\alpha_k^* = 0$ are \emph{easier} to freeze (effective threshold
$\tau_{i^*} - 2y_k\varepsilon/100 < \tau_{i^*}$), while variables
$\alpha_k^* = C_k$ are \emph{harder} to freeze (effective threshold
$\tau_{j^*} - 2y_k\varepsilon/100 < \tau_{j^*}$, which is more negative).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma 3 to describe the shift in the freezing threshold relative to the symmetric unshifted threshold (or the standard SVR case) rather than asserting an invalid direct comparison between cross-matched \alpha and \alpha^* boundary criteria.
issues.overall_effect: The comparative narrative and claim in Lemma 3 about relative ease of freezing between corresponding \alpha and \alpha^* variables is invalid as stated.
issues.title: Invalid comparison with cross-matched criteria in shrinking asymmetry lemma
issues.why_classification: The algebraic relations (20c-rewritten) and (20d-rewritten) are correct; modifying the comparative explanation leaves all algorithmic steps and guarantees intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 executes a single `for` loop (lines 4-23). The unshrinking check on lines 24-29 occurs after the loop has already terminated. Line 28 specifies `continue outer loop`, but no outer loop encloses lines 4-29. As a result, the control flow is invalid: an execution hitting this branch either errors out or falls through to lines 30-31, returning a solution that violates \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}-optimality on the full set.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the inner working-set loop and reconstruction step in an outer loop (e.g., `repeat ... until \Delta^{\mathrm{full}} \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}`) so that resetting \Aactive restarts optimization on the full training set as described in Section 7.3.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm pseudocode fails to re-enter the optimization loop upon finding KKT violations on the full variable set, undermining finite termination guarantees to \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}-optimality.
issues.title: Missing outer loop structure in Algorithm 1 makes unshrinking branch ill-defined
issues.why_classification: Enclosing the pseudocode in a standard outer loop is a routine, local fix that aligns the pseudocode with the text of Section 7.3 without changing any underlying mathematics.

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that \Omega^*, defined by \Omega^*_{k\ell} = K(\mathbf{x}_k, -\mathbf{x}_\ell), is positive semi-definite. This is false. For example, for the Gaussian RBF kernel K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}') = \exp(-\gamma\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}'\|^2) with N=2 and training points x_1 = 1, x_2 = -1, the matrix is \Omega^* = [e^{-4\gamma}, 1; 1, e^{-4\gamma}]. Its determinant is e^{-8\gamma} - 1 < 0, so \Omega^* is indefinite with one strictly negative eigenvalue.

failure_location.quote: For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$ follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect claim that \Omega^* \succeq 0 with the direct proof that \Omega_s is PSD via the feature representation \varphi_s(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\varphi(\mathbf{x}) + \varphi(-\mathbf{x})).
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification for \Omega_s \succeq 0 when a = +1 fails, although \Omega_s itself remains PSD because \mathbf{v}^\top \Omega_s \mathbf{v} = \frac{1}{4}\|\sum_k v_k(\varphi(\mathbf{x}_k) + \varphi(-\mathbf{x}_k))\|^2 \ge 0.
issues.title: False claim that the cross-reflection kernel matrix is positive semi-definite
issues.why_classification: The result \Omega_s \succeq 0 is true and easily substantiated by a standard one-line feature-space argument; no downstream claims or guarantees are lost.
